findings.claim: Velocity L-infinity blow-up implies every summand of the momentum residual diverges.
findings.reason: The implication is not valid in general, and the manuscript explicitly allows divergent individual terms whose sum and derivatives extend smoothly.

findings.claim: The five-moment system is the only cancellation mechanism in the manuscript.
findings.reason: The manuscript describes a multi-stage correction architecture including pulse stress cancellation, signed amplitudes, auxiliary-time inversion, pressure/mean correction, radial corrections, cutoffs, and residual recomputation. The five radial equations are one explicit correction step.

findings.claim: force_smooth is derived from an unlinked or free-standing NativeBounds interface.
findings.reason: The force is built from a traced actual residual. Smoothness consumes the actual derivative recurrence and locally uniform residual-jet limits. The selected assembly supplies physicalData, actualStageEstimates, and a schedule containing VanishingJointJets.

findings.claim: The final selected endpoint proves the paper-specific five-observable transport identity.
findings.reason: Witness packages the selected sums, extensions, forcing, CandidateProperties, CandidateConsequences, derivative limits, and blow-up, but no inspected declaration identifies the final activated Cartesian observables with (M,I,J,S,Cp). Intermediate barMoment and FiveRows identities are not definitionally final-field identities.

findings.claim: The missing endpoint identity alone proves the selected force is nonsmooth or Fefferman Alternative (C) is false.
findings.reason: Non-entailment at the Witness type is a paper-to-code correspondence gap, not a value-level counterexample. A selected mismatch, impossibility theorem, or failed residual bound has not been derived.
